records.source: דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּ֑הוּ מִן־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֔וֹת בְּאֶ֖רֶץ בִּנְיָמִֽן׃
records.gloss: [The] words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, of the priests who [were] in Anathoth in [the] land of Benjamin,
pieces: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin,

L.1: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, of the priests who [were] in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin,

R.1: These are the words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah. Jeremiah came from a family of priests who lived in the town of Anathoth, in the land of the tribe of Benjamin.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew (Masoretic) text of Jeremiah, which is longer than the Greek and arranges part of the book differently
alternatives: follow the shorter Greek form and its order of chapters
decisions.reason: This translation follows the Hebrew text of Jeremiah throughout. The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation, gives a form of the book about one-eighth shorter. It lacks many words and phrases and some whole passages (for example 33:14-26 and most of 39:4-13), and it places the oracles against the nations (chapters 46-51 in the Hebrew) in the middle of chapter 25, after 25:13, and in a different order. Hebrew fragments of Jeremiah found at Qumran include both a shorter form close to the Greek and the longer form, so both forms of the book were copied in ancient times. The difference shows even here: the Greek opens "The word of God that came to Jeremiah". Later decisions mention a Greek reading only where it bears on the sense (see 25:13 and 46:1).

decisions.choice: of the priests: Jeremiah came from a priestly family
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes Jeremiah's family, so that he was of priestly descent; it could describe Hilkiah alone, but either way the family was priestly. Jeremiah is never shown serving as a priest. This Hilkiah is probably not the high priest of the same name in Josiah's reign (2 Kings 22:4), who served in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Anathoth: a town of priests in Benjamin, a few miles north-east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Anathoth was one of the towns given to the priests in the territory of Benjamin (Joshua 21:18). Solomon sent the priest Abiathar home there in disgrace (1 Kings 2:26). Jeremiah later bought a field there (32:7-9), and men of his own town plotted against him (11:21-23).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (Literal, Balanced); separate sentences (Readable)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are one Hebrew sentence, the heading of the book. Literal and Balanced keep it as one sentence running into verses 2 and 3. Readable breaks it into short sentences and supplies "These are", "came from a family of" and "the town of" to make the heading plain.

records.heading: The words of Jeremiah

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו בִּימֵ֛י יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה בִּשְׁלֹשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה לְמָלְכֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: who came [the] word of Yahweh to him in [the] days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in [the] thirteenth year of his reigning,
pieces: to whom the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came during the reign of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of Josiah's reign,

L.2: to whom the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign,

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} began to give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messages to Jeremiah while Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, in Josiah's thirteenth year as king.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came to him: Yahweh gave him his message
decisions.reason: The phrase, common in Jeremiah, presents the prophet's message as given to him by God, not thought up by him (compare verse 4; 2 Samuel 7:4; Hosea 1:1). "The word" here is the message as a whole.

decisions.choice: the thirteenth year of Josiah: about 627 BC
decisions.reason: Josiah reigned thirty-one years (2 Kings 22:1). His thirteenth year was about 627 BC, five years before the book of the law was found in the temple in his eighteenth year (2 Kings 22:3-8). Jeremiah himself counts his years of preaching from this year (25:3).

decisions.choice: began to give his messages
decisions.reason: Readable says "began" because verse 3 goes on to say how long the messages continued.

decisions.choice: during the reign of ... in the thirteenth year of Josiah's reign (Balanced); while ... was king ... thirteenth year as king (Readable)
decisions.reason: This is the book-wide wording for the dated headings of Jeremiah ("in the days of", "in the Nth year of"). Verse 3 and the later headings use it too.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בִּימֵ֨י יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַד־תֹּם֙ עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְצִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה עַד־גְּל֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִֽׁי׃ס
records.gloss: and it came in [the] days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until [the] end of [the] eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until [the] exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.
pieces: and it came during the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of the reign of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, the year Jerusalem went into exile, in the fifth month.

L.3: and it came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} kept speaking to Jeremiah while Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah. These messages went on until the end of Zedekiah's eleventh year as king of Judah. Zedekiah was another son of Josiah. In the fifth month of that year, the people of Jerusalem were taken away as captives.

decisions.choice: it came: the word of Yahweh, the subject carried over from verse 2
decisions.reason: The verb has no new subject; it continues "the word of Yahweh came" from verse 2. The heading thus covers Jeremiah's preaching across three reigns.

decisions.choice: Jehoiakim and Zedekiah: the reigns named, and two short reigns left out
decisions.reason: The heading names the three kings whose reigns were long: Josiah, Jehoiakim (609-598 BC) and Zedekiah (597-586 BC), both sons of Josiah. It passes over Jehoahaz and Jehoiachin, who each reigned three months (2 Kings 23:31; 24:8).

decisions.choice: the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month: the fall of the city in 586 BC
decisions.reason: In the fifth month of Zedekiah's eleventh year the Babylonians burned the temple and took the people of Jerusalem into exile (2 Kings 25:8-11; Jeremiah 52:12-15). Jeremiah went on speaking after this (chapters 40-44); the heading marks the span of his work under Judah's last kings.

decisions.choice: kept speaking ... These messages went on (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the same word of the LORD went on coming to Jeremiah (see m1), and says in a separate sentence that Zedekiah was another son of Josiah. Balanced keeps "it came" and uses the heading wording of verse 2.

records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying,
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.4: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: to me: the book now speaks in Jeremiah's own voice
decisions.reason: After the heading in the third person (verses 1-3), Jeremiah tells of his call himself. The same first-person telling runs through the visions of verses 11-19.

decisions.choice: came to me, saying: (Literal); came to me: (Balanced); gave me this message: (Readable)
decisions.reason: This formula returns many times in Jeremiah, and each level keeps one wording for it throughout the book.

records.heading: Jeremiah is called to be a prophet

records.source: בְּטֶ֨רֶם אֶצָּרְךָ֤ בַבֶּ֨טֶן֙ יְדַעְתִּ֔יךָ וּבְטֶ֛רֶם תֵּצֵ֥א מֵרֶ֖חֶם הִקְדַּשְׁתִּ֑יךָ נָבִ֥יא לַגּוֹיִ֖ם נְתַתִּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Before I formed you in the belly I knew you, and before you came out from [the] womb I consecrated you; a prophet to the nations I gave you.
pieces: "I knew you before I shaped you in the womb; \q I set you apart before you came out of the womb; \q I have given you to the nations as a prophet."

L.5: "Before I formed you in the belly I knew you, \q and before you came out from the womb I consecrated you; \q a prophet to the nations I appointed you."

R.5: "I knew you before I formed your body inside your mother. \q Before you were born, I chose you for a holy task. \q I made you a prophet to the nations."

decisions.choice: I knew you: I chose you and took you as my own
decisions.reason: To "know" someone in Hebrew can mean to choose him and bind him to oneself (Genesis 18:19; Amos 3:2). God's knowing Jeremiah came before Jeremiah was formed, so it rests on God's choice, not on anything Jeremiah had done.

decisions.choice: I formed you in the belly: God shaping a person, as a potter shapes clay
decisions.reason: The verb is the potter's word (18:4-6) and the word for God forming the first man (Genesis 2:7). The servant in Isaiah is also called and formed from the womb (Isaiah 49:1, 5), and Paul speaks of his own call in the same terms (Galatians 1:15).

decisions.choice: I consecrated you: set you apart as holy for my service
decisions.reason: The verb is used for setting apart priests and holy things for God (Exodus 28:41; 29:44). Jeremiah, of a priestly family (verse 1), is set apart for another service, as a prophet.

decisions.choice: a prophet to the nations I gave you: appointed you as a prophet whose word reaches the nations
decisions.reason: The verb is "give", used here as "appoint, make" (as in verse 18). Jeremiah's message concerns not Judah alone but other nations too (verse 10; 25:15-38; chapters 46-51).

decisions.choice: set you apart (Balanced); chose you for a holy task (Readable); given you to the nations as a prophet (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "consecrated". Balanced and Readable say what consecrating means for a person. Balanced keeps the verb "give" of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: verses 5 and 10 and the speech of verses 15-19 set in lines
decisions.reason: These words of God have the balanced, parallel lines of Hebrew verse, and the accents divide them as verse. They are set in lines inside the prose account of the call; the story around them stays prose.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה לֹא־יָדַ֖עְתִּי דַּבֵּ֑רכִּי־נַ֖עַר אָנֹֽכִי׃פ
records.gloss: And I said, ah, Lord Yahweh, look, not I know to speak, for a youth I [am].
pieces: I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! I do not know how to speak; I am a mere youth."

L.6: And I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Look, I do not know [how] to speak, for a youth I [am]."

R.6: I answered, "Oh no, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! I do not know how to speak well. I am still young."

decisions.choice: a youth: a boy or young man, not yet of an age to speak with authority
decisions.reason: The word covers a wide range, from a baby (Exodus 2:6) to a young man of fighting age (2 Samuel 18:5). Jeremiah's exact age is not known. The point is that he is too young and untried to be heeded by elders and kings; Solomon says the same of himself (1 Kings 3:7).

decisions.choice: ah: a cry of dismay addressed to God
decisions.reason: The same cry is heard from Joshua (Joshua 7:7), Gideon (Judges 6:22) and Ezekiel (Ezekiel 4:14), each time protesting or fearing before God.

decisions.choice: I do not know how to speak: an objection like that of Moses
decisions.reason: Moses pleaded that he was not a man of words (Exodus 4:10). God answers Jeremiah as he answered Moses, by promising to give him the words (verses 7-9; Exodus 4:11-12).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the title Adonai ("Lord") followed by the divine name. Writing the name as GOD after "Lord" avoids "Lord LORD", as in Isaiah.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י אַל־תֹּאמַ֖ר נַ֣עַר אָנֹ֑כִי כִּ֠י עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֙ תֵּלֵ֔ךְ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲצַוְּךָ֖ תְּדַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, do not say, a youth I [am], for to all whom I send you you will go, and all that I command you you will speak.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not say, 'I am a mere youth.' To all the people I send you to, you will go; every word I command you, you will speak.

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not say, 'A youth I [am],' for to everyone to whom I send you, you will go, and all that I command you, you will speak.

R.7: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Do not say, 'I am still young.' When I send you to people, you must go. When I give you a message, you must speak it.

decisions.choice: to all to whom I send you: to every person I send you to
alternatives: on every errand I send you
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read as "to all the people to whom I send you" or as "on every errand I send you". Both say that God's sending, not Jeremiah's age, decides where he goes.

decisions.choice: all that I command you: the prophet's authority rests on God's command
decisions.reason: God does not deny that Jeremiah is young. He answers that the message and the sending are his, as he told Moses (Exodus 4:11-12; Deuteronomy 18:18).

decisions.choice: When I send you to people, you must go. When I give you a message, you must speak it.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the two long clauses into short sentences with the same sense.

records.source: אַל־תִּירָ֖א מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Do not be afraid of their faces, for with you I [am] to deliver you, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Have no fear of them, for I am with you to rescue you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.8: Do not be afraid of their faces, for with you I [am] to deliver you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.8: Do not be afraid of them. I am with you, and I will keep you safe, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: afraid of their faces: afraid of them, afraid to face them
decisions.reason: "Face" here stands for the people themselves as they confront the prophet. They are the people to whom he is sent (verse 7), named in verse 18.

decisions.choice: I am with you: God's promise of his presence to the one he sends
decisions.reason: God made the same promise to Isaac (Genesis 26:3), Moses (Exodus 3:12) and Gideon (Judges 6:16). It returns at the end of the chapter (verse 19), framing the whole call.

decisions.choice: declares Yahweh: a formula marking the words as Yahweh's own
decisions.reason: The noun means "an utterance"; the formula seals what precedes as the LORD's own declaration. It is very frequent in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: rescue (Balanced); keep you safe (Readable); deliver (Literal)
decisions.reason: The verb means to snatch someone out of danger. The same wording is used in verse 19.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ וַיַּגַּ֖ע עַל־פִּ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י הִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי דְבָרַ֖י בְּפִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And stretched out Yahweh his hand and made touch on my mouth, and said Yahweh to me, look, I have put my words in your mouth.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} then stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and laid it on my mouth, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "There: I have placed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth.

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and made [it] touch my mouth, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Look, I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words in your mouth.

R.9: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched my mouth. He said to me, "Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words are in your mouth. I have put them there.

decisions.choice: touched my mouth: a sign that God himself prepares the prophet to speak
decisions.reason: Isaiah's lips were touched with a coal from the altar (Isaiah 6:7), and Ezekiel was given a scroll to eat (Ezekiel 3:1-3). Here the LORD's own hand touches Jeremiah's mouth, answering his fear that he cannot speak (verse 6).

decisions.choice: I have put my words in your mouth: the promise of a prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: God promised to raise up a prophet like Moses and said, "I will put my words in his mouth" (Deuteronomy 18:18). Jeremiah is that kind of prophet: he will speak only what God gives him (5:14; 15:19).

decisions.choice: I have put: done now, in this very act
decisions.reason: The verb describes what God does as he speaks. From this moment Jeremiah's words are God's words.

decisions.choice: Look (Literal); There (Balanced); Now (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word points to what has just happened. Balanced and Readable choose words that point to the moment of the touch.

records.source: רְאֵ֞ה הִפְקַדְתִּ֣יךָ׀הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה עַל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ וְעַל־הַמַּמְלָכ֔וֹת לִנְת֥וֹשׁ וְלִנְת֖וֹץ וּלְהַאֲבִ֣יד וְלַהֲר֑וֹס לִבְנ֖וֹת וְלִנְטֽוֹעַ׃פ
records.gloss: See, I have appointed you the day this over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down and to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant.
pieces: See, on this day I have set you over nations and over kingdoms, \q to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and overthrow, \q to build and plant."

L.10: See, I have appointed you this day over the nations and over the kingdoms, \q to uproot and to tear down, and to destroy and to overthrow, \q to build and to plant."

R.10: Look! Today I am giving you authority over nations and kingdoms. \q You will uproot and tear down, destroy and overthrow. \q You will build and plant."

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, destroy, overthrow, build, plant: four words of judgment and two of restoration
decisions.reason: The pictures come from farming and building: plants pulled up and buildings pulled down, then buildings put up and trees planted. Judgment comes first and takes up most of the line, but the last word is building and planting. The pairs return through the book (18:7-9; 24:6; 31:28; 42:10; 45:4).

decisions.choice: appointed you over the nations: authority exercised through the word God has given
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone in charge. Jeremiah holds no throne or army; he uproots and builds by speaking the word God put in his mouth (verse 9), and God carries it out (verse 12).

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, destroy, overthrow, build, plant
decisions.reason: Each level keeps these six English verbs wherever the list or part of it returns in Jeremiah, so the reader can hear the echo of this verse.

decisions.choice: giving you authority ... You will
decisions.reason: Readable says what being set over the nations means and turns the purpose clauses into plain statements of what Jeremiah will do.

decisions.choice: to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and plant
decisions.reason: Balanced drops the repeated "to" in the last two pairs, as natural English lists do. The six verbs and their order stay the same (r-en-1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֔ר מָה־אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וָאֹמַ֕ר מַקֵּ֥ל שָׁקֵ֖ד אֲנִ֥י רֹאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying, what [are] you seeing, Jeremiah? And I said, a rod of almond I [am] seeing.
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "I see a rod cut from an almond tree."

L.11: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying: "What [are] you seeing, Jeremiah?" And I said, "A rod of almond I [am] seeing."

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "I see a stick from an almond tree."

decisions.choice: a rod: a stick or staff cut from a tree
decisions.reason: The word means a stick, rod or staff (Genesis 30:37; Numbers 22:27; 1 Samuel 17:40). Nothing is said of buds or blossoms; what matters is the name of the tree (verse 12).

decisions.choice: almond: the tree that wakes first
decisions.reason: The almond is the first tree in the land to blossom, in late winter, while other trees still look dead. Aaron's staff, which sprouted overnight, bore almonds (Numbers 17:23). Its name sounds like the word for "watching" (see verse 12).

decisions.choice: What do you see?: a vision explained by God's question and answer
decisions.reason: God asks the prophet to name what he sees and then explains it, as he does with Amos (Amos 7:8; 8:2) and later with Jeremiah (24:3).

decisions.choice: a rod cut from an almond tree (Balanced); a stick from an almond tree (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that this is a cut stick, not a living branch on the tree.

records.heading: An almond rod and a boiling pot

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י הֵיטַ֣בְתָּ לִרְא֑וֹת כִּֽי־שֹׁקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י עַל־דְּבָרִ֖י לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, you have done well to see, for watching I [am] over my word to do it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "You have seen rightly, for I am keeping watch over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word until I carry it out."

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "You have done well to see, for watching I [am] over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word to do it."

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "You are right. The name of the almond tree sounds like the word for 'watching.' And I am watching over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word to make sure it comes true."

decisions.choice: watching: a play on the name of the almond tree in verse 11
alternatives: the almond as a sign that the word will come early or soon
decisions.reason: The almond tree is called *shaqed*, and "watching, keeping awake" is *shoqed*: the two words sound almost the same. The vision works through this sound. As the almond is the tree awake first, so the LORD is awake and watching over his word. The play on words cannot be kept in most translations; the sense is given and the link explained.

decisions.choice: you have done well to see: you have seen correctly
decisions.reason: The phrase approves Jeremiah's answer: he has named the thing rightly, and the name is the key to the message.

decisions.choice: watching over my word to do it: God himself makes his word come true
decisions.reason: What God says through the prophet does not fail (Isaiah 55:11). The same verb returns in 31:28: as God watched over Israel to uproot and tear down, so he will watch over them to build and to plant (compare verse 10).

decisions.choice: The name of the almond tree sounds like the word for 'watching.'
decisions.reason: Readable puts the explanation of the play on words into the text, since without it the reader cannot see why the almond tree matters (see m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה׀אֵלַי֙ שֵׁנִ֣ית לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר סִ֤יר נָפ֨וּחַ֙ אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֔ה וּפָנָ֖יו מִפְּנֵ֥י צָפֽוֹנָה׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me a second [time], saying, what [are] you seeing? And I said, a pot blown upon I [am] seeing, and its face [is] from [the] face of [the] north.
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me a second time: "What do you see?" I said, "I see a pot fanned to a boil, its mouth tilted from the north toward the south."

L.13: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me a second [time], saying: "What [are] you seeing?" And I said, "A pot blown upon I [am] seeing, and its face [is] from the face of the north."

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me a second message: "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a pot boiling hard over a hot fire. It is tipping from the north side, about to spill toward the south."

decisions.choice: blown upon: a pot over a fire fanned by blowing, so boiling hard
decisions.reason: The word means "blown on", of a fire made hotter by blowing (compare Job 41:12; Ezekiel 22:20-21). The pot is seething and about to boil over.

decisions.choice: its face from the face of the north: its mouth tilted away from the north, so that it pours out southward
alternatives: the pot is set facing away from the north
decisions.reason: The "face" of a pot is its front or mouth. The phrase most likely means that the pot stands in the north and is tipped to spill toward the south, onto Judah, as verse 14 explains. It could also mean simply that the pot faces from the north. The general sense, disaster coming from the north, is clear either way.

decisions.choice: toward the south (Balanced); about to spill toward the south (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where a pot tilted away from the north will spill, following verse 14. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י מִצָּפוֹן֙ תִּפָּתַ֣ח הָרָעָ֔ה עַ֥ל כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, from [the] north will be opened the disaster on all [the] inhabitants of the land.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "From the north, disaster will burst out upon everyone who lives in the land.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "From the north the disaster will be let loose on all the inhabitants of the land.

R.14: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Trouble will burst out from the north. It will fall on everyone who lives in this land.

decisions.choice: from the north: the road by which invaders came into Judah
decisions.reason: The desert east of Judah blocked the direct way from Mesopotamia, so armies from Assyria and Babylon came down through Syria and entered the land from the north. The enemy is not named here; later the book names Babylon (20:4; 25:9).

decisions.choice: the disaster: calamity, harm
decisions.reason: The word can mean moral evil or harm that falls on people. Here it is the disaster of invasion. The same word names the people's "wickedness" in verse 16: their evil brings evil on them.

decisions.choice: will be let loose: will break open and pour out
decisions.reason: The verb is "be opened". The disaster bursts out like the contents of the tilted pot (verse 13), or like waters let loose.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Judah
decisions.reason: The same word can mean the whole earth, but verse 15 shows that the land of Judah and its capital are meant.

decisions.choice: Trouble ... this land
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the disaster and says "this land" to make clear it is Judah (see m4).

records.source: כִּ֣י׀הִנְנִ֣י קֹרֵ֗א לְכָֽל־מִשְׁפְּח֛וֹת מַמְלְכ֥וֹת צָפ֖וֹנָה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וּבָ֡אוּ וְֽנָתְנוּ֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּסְא֜וֹ פֶּ֣תַח׀שַׁעֲרֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם וְעַ֤ל כָּל־חוֹמֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ סָבִ֔יב וְעַ֖ל כָּל־עָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: For look, I [am] calling to all [the] clans of [the] kingdoms of [the] north, declares Yahweh, and they will come and set each his throne [at the] entrance of [the] gates of Jerusalem, and against all its walls around, and against all [the] cities of Judah.
pieces: For I am about to summon all the clans of the northern kingdoms, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q They will come, and each of them will set up his throne at the entrance of Jerusalem's gates, against all its surrounding walls, \q and against all the towns of Judah.

L.15: For look, I [am] calling to all the clans of the kingdoms of the north, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q and they will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all its walls all around, \q and against all the cities of Judah.

R.15: I am about to call all the peoples of the kingdoms in the north, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Their kings will come and place their thrones at the gates of Jerusalem. \q They will attack all the walls around the city and all the towns of Judah.

decisions.choice: the clans of the kingdoms of the north: the peoples that make up the northern powers
decisions.reason: "Clans" are the family groups that formed a people. The kingdoms are not named; Babylon and the peoples under its rule are later named as God's instrument (25:9).

decisions.choice: each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates: conquerors sitting as judges over the city
decisions.reason: The city gate was where judgment was given (Deuteronomy 21:19; Ruth 4:1-2). Enemy rulers setting their thrones there will sit in judgment over Jerusalem. It came true when the officers of the king of Babylon sat in the Middle Gate (39:3).

decisions.choice: against all its walls ... against all the cities of Judah: the invaders set against the city and the towns
decisions.reason: The preposition here means "against": the northern rulers come in hostility, besieging Jerusalem's walls and the towns of Judah.

decisions.choice: Their kings ... They will attack
decisions.reason: Readable says who sits on the thrones and what "against" the walls and towns means (see m3). It says "peoples" for "clans" because the clans here stand for whole nations.

records.source: וְדִבַּרְתִּ֤י מִשְׁפָּטַי֙ אוֹתָ֔ם עַ֖ל כָּל־רָעָתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָב֗וּנִי וַֽיְקַטְּרוּ֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לְמַעֲשֵׂ֥י יְדֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will speak my judgments [against] them for all their evil, who have forsaken me and made smoke to gods other and bowed down to [the] works of their hands.
pieces: I will pronounce {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sentence on them for all their wickedness, \q because they have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, burned offerings to other gods, and bowed down to what their own hands have made.

L.16: And I will speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments against them for all their evil, \q who have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and made offerings smoke to other gods and bowed down to the works of their [own] hands.

R.16: I will announce {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgment on the people of Judah for all the evil they have done. \q They have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They have burned offerings to other gods and worshiped idols they made with their own hands.

decisions.choice: speak my judgments against them: pass sentence on them as a judge
decisions.reason: The same expression is used when the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah (39:5; 52:9). God himself is the judge; the rulers of verse 15 carry out his sentence.

decisions.choice: them: the people of Judah and Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "Them" and "their evil" refer to the people of the land in verse 14 and the city and towns of verse 15, not to the invaders.

decisions.choice: made smoke: burned offerings or incense to other gods
decisions.reason: The verb means "to make smoke rise" and is used of burning sacrifices and incense. Jeremiah uses it often of offerings to other gods (7:9; 11:13; 44:17).

decisions.choice: the works of their hands: idols they had made themselves
decisions.reason: To bow down to what one's own hands have made is the folly the prophets mock (Isaiah 2:8; Psalm 115:4). Forsaking the LORD and worshiping idols is the root of all the evil the verse names.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah ... idols
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are (see m2) and what "the works of their hands" are (see m4).

records.source: וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֔יךָ וְקַמְתָּ֙ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֑ךָּ אַל־תֵּחַת֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם פֶּֽן־אֲחִתְּךָ֖ לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, you will gird up your loins and arise and speak to them all that I command you; do not be dismayed before them, lest I dismay you before them.
pieces: As for you, tuck your robe into your belt, get up, and tell them everything I command you. \q Do not be shattered by them, or I will shatter you in front of them.

L.17: And you, you will gird up your loins and arise and speak to them all that I command you. \q Do not be dismayed before them, lest I dismay you before them.

R.17: Now get ready for action! Stand up and tell them everything I command you. \q Do not let them fill you with terror, or I will fill you with terror in front of them.

decisions.choice: gird up your loins: tuck up your long robe into your belt, ready for action
decisions.reason: People wore long robes and tucked them into a belt to run, work or fight (1 Kings 18:46; 2 Kings 4:29; Job 38:3). God tells Jeremiah to get ready for the hard task ahead.

decisions.choice: be dismayed ... dismay you: be shattered with fear, and be shattered
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice: if Jeremiah gives way to fear of the people, God will let him be broken before them. The word means to be shattered, crushed with fear.

decisions.choice: you will gird up: a command
decisions.reason: The verbs are in a form that often gives instructions; here they tell Jeremiah what to do, in contrast with what God will do in verse 18.

decisions.choice: tuck your robe into your belt (Balanced); get ready for action (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture, worded as in 1 Kings 18:46; Readable gives its meaning.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֞י הִנֵּ֧ה נְתַתִּ֣יךָ הַיּ֗וֹם לְעִ֨יר מִבְצָ֜ר וּלְעַמּ֥וּד בַּרְזֶ֛ל וּלְחֹמ֥וֹת נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ לְמַלְכֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ לְשָׂרֶ֔יהָ לְכֹהֲנֶ֖יהָ וּלְעַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I, look, I have made you the day [this] into a city of fortification and into a pillar of iron and into walls of bronze against all the land, to [the] kings of Judah, to its princes, to its priests and to [the] people of the land.
pieces: And I, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} part, have made you today a walled city, a pillar of iron, and walls of bronze, set against the whole land: \q against Judah's kings and officials, its priests, and the people of the land.

L.18: And I, look, I have made you this day into a fortified city and into a pillar of iron and into walls of bronze against all the land, \q against the kings of Judah, against its princes, against its priests, and against the people of the land.

R.18: Today I am making you as hard to defeat as a city with strong walls, an iron pillar or walls of bronze. \q You will stand against everyone in the land: the kings of Judah, its leaders, its priests and all its people.

decisions.choice: a fortified city, a pillar of iron, walls of bronze: strength that cannot be broken
decisions.reason: The pictures do not promise that Jeremiah will not be attacked, but that he will stand firm when he is (verse 19). God repeats the promise of bronze walls when Jeremiah is near despair (15:20).

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase names the landholding people of Judah, who had a voice in public affairs and even made kings (2 Kings 21:24; 23:30). Here they stand beside the kings, officials and priests: the whole nation.

decisions.choice: I have made you: already decided and done
decisions.reason: As in verse 10 ("I have appointed"), God speaks of his decision as already done, though Jeremiah will live it out over many years.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means the royal officials and leading men of Judah; each level uses the wording it has elsewhere.

decisions.choice: as hard to defeat as
decisions.reason: Readable turns the pictures into a comparison so the reader sees what they mean (see m1).

records.source: וְנִלְחֲמ֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹא־י֣וּכְלוּ לָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ׃פ
records.gloss: And they will fight against you, but not they will prevail against you, for with you I [am], declares Yahweh, to deliver you.
pieces: They will make war on you, but they will not overcome you, \q for I am with you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to rescue you."

L.19: And they will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, \q for with you I [am], declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to deliver you."

R.19: They will fight against you, but they will not defeat you. \q I am with you, and I will keep you safe, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: for with you I am ... to deliver you: the promise of verse 8 repeated
decisions.reason: The call ends with the same promise with which it began (verse 8), and 15:20 repeats this verse almost word for word when Jeremiah complains to God.

decisions.choice: prevail against you: overpower you
decisions.reason: The verb means to be able, to have the power; with "against" it means to win the struggle (Genesis 32:26; Psalm 129:2).

decisions.choice: to rescue you (Balanced); I will keep you safe (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, so the two promises read alike.
